title: 08. Files & Errors: CSV Files — Complete Guide
summary: CSV (Comma-Separated Values) is the universal language of spreadsheets . Every database, Excel, and data tool can read/write CSV.

sections.title: Concept Explanation (Junior Developer Style)
sections.body:
**CSV** (Comma-Separated Values) is the **universal language of spreadsheets** 📊. Every database, Excel, and data tool can read/write CSV. Think of it like a simple table:

```
name,age,city,salary
Alice,30,New York,75000
Bob,25,London,65000
Charlie,35,Tokyo,90000
```

> 🧠 **Why use Python's `csv` module** instead of manual splitting?
>
> - Handles **quoted fields** with commas: `"Smith, John",30`
> - Handles **newlines inside fields**: `"Line1\nLine2",30`
> - Handles **different delimiters**: `;`, `\t`, `|`
> - Much safer than `line.split(",")`

### Four Core CSV Tools:

```python
import csv

csv.reader(file)         # Read rows as LISTS
csv.writer(file)         # Write rows from LISTS
csv.DictReader(file)     # Read rows as DICTS (uses header)
csv.DictWriter(file)     # Write rows from DICTS
```

sections.title: 5 Examples
sections.body:
```python
# ── Example 1: csv.writer and csv.reader — basic ──────────────────────
import csv
import os

# WRITING with csv.writer
with open("employees.csv", "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    # newline="" is REQUIRED for csv module on all platforms!
    writer = csv.writer(f)

    # Write header
    writer.writerow(["Name", "Age", "Department", "Salary", "City"])

    # Write data rows
    writer.writerow(["Alice Johnson", 30, "Engineering", 85000, "New York"])
    writer.writerow(["Bob Smith", 25, "Marketing", 65000, "London"])
    writer.writerow(["Charlie, Jr.", 35, "Finance", 90000, "Tokyo"])  # comma in name!
    writer.writerow(["Diana O'Brien", 28, "HR", 70000, "Sydney"])

    # Write multiple rows at once
    extra_rows = [
        ["Eve Wilson", 32, "Engineering", 95000, "San Francisco"],
        ["Frank Lee", 27, "Design", 72000, "Seattle"],
    ]
    writer.writerows(extra_rows)

print("Written employees.csv:")

# READING with csv.reader
with open("employees.csv", "r", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    reader = csv.reader(f)

    header = next(reader)  # Read header row
    print(f"Columns: {header}")
    print("-" * 60)

    for row in reader:
        # row is a LIST of strings
        name, age, dept, salary, city = row
        print(f"  {name:<20} {age:<5} {dept:<15} ${int(salary):>8,} {city}")

os.remove("employees.csv")
```

```python
# ── Example 2: csv.DictReader and csv.DictWriter — BEST PRACTICE ─────
import csv
import os

# WRITING with DictWriter — use column names, order doesn't matter!
fieldnames = ["employee_id", "name", "department", "salary", "email", "active"]

employees = [
    {"employee_id": "E001", "name": "Alice Johnson",
     "department": "Engineering", "salary": 85000,
     "email": "alice@company.com", "active": True},
    {"employee_id": "E002", "name": "Bob Smith",
     "department": "Marketing", "salary": 65000,
     "email": "bob@company.com", "active": True},
    {"employee_id": "E003", "name": "Charlie Brown",
     "department": "Finance", "salary": 90000,
     "email": "charlie@company.com", "active": False},
]

with open("employees_dict.csv", "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fieldnames)

    writer.writeheader()       # Writes the header row automatically
    writer.writerows(employees) # Write all rows at once

print("Written with DictWriter:")
print(open("employees_dict.csv").read())

# READING with DictReader — each row is an OrderedDict/dict
print("\nReading with DictReader:")
with open("employees_dict.csv", "r", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    reader = csv.DictReader(f)  # First row automatically becomes headers

    for row in reader:
        # row is a dict — access by column name (much more readable!)
        print(f"  ID: {row['employee_id']}"
              f"  Name: {row['name']:<20}"
              f"  Salary: ${int(row['salary']):>8,}"
              f"  Active: {row['active']}")

os.remove("employees_dict.csv")
```

```python
# ── Example 3: CSV with different delimiters and options ───────────────
import csv
import io
import os

# Custom delimiter — semicolons (common in European CSV)
data = [
    ["Product", "Price (EUR)", "Category", "In Stock"],
    ["Laptop Pro", "1299,99", "Electronics", "Yes"],  # comma in price!
    ["USB-C Hub", "49,99", "Accessories", "No"],
    ["Monitor 4K", "799,00", "Electronics", "Yes"],
]

# Write with semicolon delimiter
with open("european.csv", "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    writer = csv.writer(f, delimiter=";")
    writer.writerows(data)

print("European CSV (semicolons):")
print(open("european.csv").read())

# Read with semicolon delimiter
with open("european.csv", "r", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    reader = csv.reader(f, delimiter=";")
    for row in reader:
        print(f"  {row}")

# Tab-separated values (TSV)
with open("data.tsv", "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    writer = csv.writer(f, delimiter="\t")  # tab delimiter
    writer.writerow(["Name", "Score", "Grade"])
    writer.writerow(["Alice", "95", "A"])
    writer.writerow(["Bob", "82", "B"])

print("\nTSV file:")
print(repr(open("data.tsv").read()))

# CSV with quoting options
with open("quoted.csv", "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    writer = csv.writer(f, quoting=csv.QUOTE_ALL)  # quote EVERYTHING
    writer.writerow(["Name", "Notes"])
    writer.writerow(["Alice", 'She said "hello, world"'])
    writer.writerow(["Bob", "Has\nnewline in note"])

print("\nQuoted CSV:")
print(open("quoted.csv").read())

for f in ["european.csv", "data.tsv", "quoted.csv"]:
    os.remove(f)
```

```python
# ── Example 4: CSV with type conversion and validation ─────────────────
import csv
import os
from datetime import datetime
from decimal import Decimal

def read_csv_with_types(filepath, type_map=None):
    """
    Read CSV and convert columns to appropriate Python types.
    type_map: dict of column_name → conversion function
    """
    type_map = type_map or {}
    records  = []
    errors   = []

    with open(filepath, "r", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        reader = csv.DictReader(f)

        for line_num, row in enumerate(reader, 2):  # 2 = data starts at line 2
            converted = {}
            row_errors = []

            for col, value in row.items():
                value = value.strip()
                converter = type_map.get(col)

                if converter:
                    try:
                        converted[col] = converter(value) if value else None
                    except (ValueError, TypeError) as e:
                        row_errors.append(f"Line {line_num}, col '{col}': {e}")
                        converted[col] = None  # use None for failed conversion
                else:
                    converted[col] = value  # keep as string

            records.append(converted)
            if row_errors:
                errors.extend(row_errors)

    return records, errors

# Create test CSV
with open("sales.csv", "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=[
        "date", "product", "quantity", "unit_price", "discount", "active"
    ])
    writer.writeheader()
    writer.writerows([
        {"date":"2024-01-15","product":"Laptop","quantity":"5",
         "unit_price":"999.99","discount":"0.10","active":"True"},
        {"date":"2024-01-16","product":"Mouse","quantity":"20",
         "unit_price":"25.50","discount":"0.05","active":"True"},
        {"date":"2024-01-17","product":"Monitor","quantity":"bad",  # error!
         "unit_price":"449.99","discount":"0.15","active":"False"},
    ])

# Read with type conversions
type_map = {
    "date":       lambda s: datetime.strptime(s, "%Y-%m-%d"),
    "quantity":   int,
    "unit_price": float,
    "discount":   float,
    "active":     lambda s: s.lower() == "true",
}

records, errors = read_csv_with_types("sales.csv", type_map)

print("Parsed records:")
for r in records:
    total = (r["quantity"] or 0) * (r["unit_price"] or 0) * (1 - (r["discount"] or 0))
    print(f"  {r['date'].strftime('%Y-%m-%d') if r['date'] else 'N/A'}"
          f"  {r['product']:<10}"
          f"  qty={r['quantity']}"
          f"  total=${total:.2f}")

if errors:
    print(f"\nErrors ({len(errors)}):")
    for err in errors:
        print(f"  ⚠️  {err}")

os.remove("sales.csv")
```

```python
# ── Example 5: Real world — CSV data processing pipeline ──────────────
import csv
import os
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import datetime

def process_sales_csv(input_file, output_file, summary_file):
    """
    Complete CSV processing pipeline:
    1. Read raw sales data
    2. Validate and clean
    3. Calculate derived fields
    4. Write processed data
    5. Write summary report
    """
    # Create test input
    with open(input_file, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=[
            "transaction_id","date","customer","product",
            "quantity","unit_price","region"
        ])
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerows([
            {"transaction_id":"T001","date":"2024-01-15",
             "customer":"Alice","product":"Laptop",
             "quantity":"2","unit_price":"999.99","region":"North"},
            {"transaction_id":"T002","date":"2024-01-15",
             "customer":"Bob","product":"Mouse",
             "quantity":"5","unit_price":"25.50","region":"South"},
            {"transaction_id":"T003","date":"2024-01-16",
             "customer":"Alice","product":"Monitor",
             "quantity":"1","unit_price":"449.99","region":"North"},
            {"transaction_id":"T004","date":"2024-01-16",
             "customer":"Charlie","product":"Laptop",
             "quantity":"bad","unit_price":"999.99","region":"East"},  # bad data
            {"transaction_id":"T005","date":"2024-01-17",
             "customer":"Diana","product":"Keyboard",
             "quantity":"3","unit_price":"79.99","region":"West"},
        ])

    processed_rows = []
    skipped_rows   = []
    summary        = {
        "by_region":   defaultdict(lambda: {"count":0,"revenue":0.0}),
        "by_product":  defaultdict(lambda: {"count":0,"revenue":0.0}),
        "by_customer": defaultdict(lambda: {"count":0,"revenue":0.0}),
        "total_revenue": 0.0,
        "total_records": 0,
        "skipped_records": 0,
    }

    with open(input_file, "r", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fin:
        reader = csv.DictReader(fin)

        for row in reader:
            summary["total_records"] += 1
            try:
                # Validate and convert
                quantity   = int(row["quantity"])
                unit_price = float(row["unit_price"])
                date       = datetime.strptime(row["date"], "%Y-%m-%d")

                # Calculate derived fields
                revenue = quantity * unit_price
                tax     = revenue * 0.08

                processed_row = {
                    **row,
                    "quantity":    quantity,
                    "unit_price":  unit_price,
                    "revenue":     round(revenue, 2),
                    "tax":         round(tax, 2),
                    "total":       round(revenue + tax, 2),
                    "month":       date.strftime("%Y-%m"),
                    "day_of_week": date.strftime("%A"),
                }
                processed_rows.append(processed_row)

                # Update summary
                region   = row["region"]
                product  = row["product"]
                customer = row["customer"]

                for key, val in [("by_region",region),
                                  ("by_product",product),
                                  ("by_customer",customer)]:
                    summary[key][val]["count"]   += 1
                    summary[key][val]["revenue"] += revenue

                summary["total_revenue"] += revenue

            except (ValueError, KeyError) as e:
                summary["skipped_records"] += 1
                skipped_rows.append({**row, "error": str(e)})

    # Write processed data
    if processed_rows:
        out_fields = list(processed_rows[0].keys())
        with open(output_file, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fout:
            writer = csv.DictWriter(fout, fieldnames=out_fields)
            writer.writeheader()
            writer.writerows(processed_rows)

    # Write summary
    with open(summary_file, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fs:
        fs.write("SALES PROCESSING SUMMARY\n")
        fs.write(f"Total Records  : {summary['total_records']}\n")
        fs.write(f"Processed      : {len(processed_rows)}\n")
        fs.write(f"Skipped        : {summary['skipped_records']}\n")
        fs.write(f"Total Revenue  : ${summary['total_revenue']:,.2f}\n\n")

        fs.write("BY REGION:\n")
        for region, data in sorted(summary["by_region"].items()):
            fs.write(f"  {region:<10}: {data['count']} sales, ${data['revenue']:,.2f}\n")

        fs.write("\nBY PRODUCT:\n")
        for product, data in sorted(summary["by_product"].items(),
                                    key=lambda x: x[1]["revenue"],
                                    reverse=True):
            fs.write(f"  {product:<12}: {data['count']} units, ${data['revenue']:,.2f}\n")

    print(f"✅ Processed: {len(processed_rows)} rows")
    print(f"⚠️  Skipped:   {len(skipped_rows)} rows")
    print(f"💰 Revenue:   ${summary['total_revenue']:,.2f}")
    print(f"\nSummary file: {summary_file}")
    print(open(summary_file).read())

process_sales_csv("raw_sales.csv", "processed_sales.csv", "sales_summary.txt")

for f in ["raw_sales.csv", "processed_sales.csv", "sales_summary.txt"]:
    if os.path.exists(f):
        os.remove(f)
```

quiz.question: Why must you use newline="" when opening files for the csv module?
options: 5-Year Exp Answer: > Five standard levels in ascending severity: DEBUG (10) — detailed diagnostic info, for development only; INFO (20) — normal operation events,…
5-Year Exp Answer: > CSV files from different systems have encoding issues: > > > > Real bug: our CSV import processed millions of records, then failed at record 500k…
5-Year Exp Answer: > f.tell() returns the current byte position of the file pointer. f.seek(offset, whence) moves the pointer. whence=0 (default) — from beginning,…
5-Year Exp Answer: > The csv module handles its own newline processing internally.
quiz.explanation: 5-Year Exp Answer: The csv module handles its own newline processing internally. If you open without newline="", Python's text mode also processes newlines — double-processing occurs. On Windows: without newline="", writing \r\n gets translated to \r\r\n (blank lines appear between rows!).

quiz.question: What is the difference between csv.reader and csv.DictReader?
options: 5-Year Exp Answer: > JSONL (JSON Lines, .jsonl) stores one valid JSON object per line.
5-Year Exp Answer: > f.tell() returns the current byte position of the file pointer. f.seek(offset, whence) moves the pointer. whence=0 (default) — from beginning,…
5-Year Exp Answer: > The second read() returns an empty string because the file pointer is already at the end of file (EOF).
5-Year Exp Answer: > csv.reader yields each row as a list — row[0], row[1], etc. csv.DictReader yields each row as a dict — row["name"], row["age"].
quiz.explanation: 5-Year Exp Answer: csv.reader yields each row as a list — row[0], row[1], etc. csv.DictReader yields each row as a dict — row["name"], row["age"]. DictReader uses the first row as keys automatically. Pros of DictReader: self-documenting code, order-independent column access, handles extra/missing columns gracefully.

options: 5-Year Exp Answer: > Use f.read(size) which reads up to size bytes: > > > > Why: (1) Memory efficiency — 10GB file, 8KB chunks = constant ~8KB memory.
5-Year Exp Answer: > Text mode ('r', 'w'): Python automatically handles encoding/decoding and newline translation (\n on Unix, \r\n on Windows).
5-Year Exp Answer: > f.tell() returns the current byte position of the file pointer. f.seek(offset, whence) moves the pointer. whence=0 (default) — from beginning,…
5-Year Exp Answer: > The csv module has built-in dialects: > > > > In practice: use csv.Sniffer() to auto-detect dialect from file sample.
quiz.explanation: 5-Year Exp Answer: The csv module has built-in dialects: In practice: use csv.Sniffer() to auto-detect dialect from file sample. I use dialect detection when processing user-uploaded CSV files from various sources — users upload files from Excel (Windows), LibreOffice (Linux), etc., all with slightly different formats. ---
